introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics Paper 2 (0765/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

questions.enonce_markdown: The first and last terms of an arithmetic progression are $7$ and $43$ respectively. The sum of the terms of the progression is $250$. Find the number of terms and the common difference of the progression. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let there be $n$ terms, first term $a = 7$, last term $l = 43$ and common difference $d$. The sum is

$$S_n = \frac{n}{2}(a + l) = \frac{n}{2}(7 + 43) = 25n = 250 \;\Longrightarrow\; n = 10.$$

The last term is $a + (n-1)d = 43$:

$$7 + 9d = 43 \;\Longrightarrow\; 9d = 36 \;\Longrightarrow\; d = 4.$$

$$\boxed{n = 10, \qquad d = 4}$$

Check: $S_{10} = \dfrac{10}{2}\bigl[2(7) + 9(4)\bigr] = 5 \times 50 = 250$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Obtain the first four terms of the binomial expansion of $\left(1 - \dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^{-2}$ and find the set of values of $x$ for which the expansion is valid.

Hence, deduce the first four terms of the binomial expansion of $(2 - 3x)^{-2}$. (7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $|u| < 1$ and any real $n$: $(1+u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2!}u^2 + \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{3!}u^3 + \cdots$. Here $n = -2$ and $u = -\dfrac32 x$.

- Term in $x$: $n u = (-2)\left(-\dfrac32 x\right) = 3x$.
- Term in $x^2$: $\dfrac{(-2)(-3)}{2}\left(-\dfrac32 x\right)^2 = 3 \times \dfrac{9}{4}x^2 = \dfrac{27}{4}x^2$.
- Term in $x^3$: $\dfrac{(-2)(-3)(-4)}{6}\left(-\dfrac32 x\right)^3 = (-4)\left(-\dfrac{27}{8}x^3\right) = \dfrac{27}{2}x^3$.

$$\boxed{\left(1 - \tfrac32 x\right)^{-2} = 1 + 3x + \tfrac{27}{4}x^2 + \tfrac{27}{2}x^3 + \cdots}$$

**Validity.** The expansion converges when $\left|-\dfrac32 x\right| < 1$, that is $|x| < \dfrac23$:

$$\left\{x : -\tfrac23 < x < \tfrac23\right\}.$$

**Hence.** Factor out $2$: $(2 - 3x) = 2\left(1 - \dfrac32 x\right)$, so

$$(2 - 3x)^{-2} = 2^{-2}\left(1 - \tfrac32 x\right)^{-2} = \frac14\left(1 + 3x + \frac{27}{4}x^2 + \frac{27}{2}x^3 + \cdots\right).$$

$$\boxed{(2 - 3x)^{-2} = \tfrac14 + \tfrac34 x + \tfrac{27}{16}x^2 + \tfrac{27}{8}x^3 + \cdots}$$

valid for the same set, $-\dfrac23 < x < \dfrac23$. Check at $x = 0.1$: exact $(2 - 0.3)^{-2} = 1/2.89 = 0.34602$; series $0.25 + 0.075 + 0.016875 + 0.003375 = 0.34525$, close (the next term is of order $10^{-3}$).
